title: Rights Are Not Real
listing_description: A political argument that treats rights not as self-executing moral facts but as protections made durable by organized power, vigilance, and institutions.
reader_hook: Take the unsettling sentence seriously, then follow its implications for culture, coercion, nonintervention, corruption, and the work of making moral claims effective.

source_excerpt.end_heading: Chapter 2 — There Is No Culture Outside Power
